log.text: Toxic Spikes up on P1's side

decisions.rationale: Dragapult outspeeds entire foe roster (213 > max 194), threatens Dragon Darts pressure + 4x Fire Blast on Scizor. Incineroar Fake Outs their speed control + Intimidate cycling. Conkeldurr's Mach Punch 4x OHKOs Weavile, 2x on Mamoswine/Excadrill. Kingambit Black Glasses cleans late with Supreme Overlord, immune to Toxapex TSpikes.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lead Dragapult+Incineroar, back Conkeldurr+Kingambit. Dragapult (213 Spe) outspeeds their whole team including Weavile (max 194) and Noivern (max 192). Fire Blast 4x into Scizor. Conkeldurr Sheer Force Expert Belt Mach Punch 4x Weavile, 2x Mamoswine/Excadrill. Incineroar Sitrus pivots with Parting Shot to reapply Intimidate. Kingambit immune to Toxic Spikes, Supreme Overlord cleanup. Opponent brought no Sun despite prior Charizard-Y; heavy Ice/Steel with Weavile/Mamoswine/Excadrill/Scizor core.

decisions.rationale: Scizor and Weavile lead with priority (Bullet Punch/Ice Shard) to control speed against Incineroar's FakeOut and Dragapult/Talonflame. Noivern's Draco Meteor OHKOs Dragapult and provides Defog. Toxapex anchors defense and spreads Toxic Spikes to punish Parting Shot pivots.
decisions.notebook: Opponent runs Parting Shot pivot core (Incineroar, Dragapult, Talonflame). Priority users Scizor/Weavile/Mamoswine guarantee speed advantage even under Trick Room. Noivern Draco Meteor OHKOs Dragapult. Excadrill Mold Breaker Earthquake hits Incineroar/Kingambit/Conkeldurr safely. Toxapex Toxic Spikes punishes every pivot. Save Excadrill and Mamoswine as series bench options for games 2-3 to adapt to revealed sets.

decisions.rationale: Neither foe has Protect. Fake Out flinches Weavile, preventing it from hitting Dragapult. Fire Blast OHKOs Scizor (123-233%). Scizor's only faster option is Bullet Punch (24-34% into Dragapult), survivable. After turn 1: Scizor KO'd, Weavile flinched at -1 Atk, 2v1 with opponent forced to reveal a back mon.

Kingambit immune to Toxic Spikes, Supreme Overlord cleanup. Opponent brought no Sun despite prior Charizard-Y; heavy Ice/Steel with Weavile/Mamoswine/Excadrill/Scizor core. Neither Weavile nor Scizor carries Protect.

decisions.rationale: Both priority moves target Dragapult, the biggest threat (Fire Blast 4x Scizor, 2x Weavile). Scizor's Technician Bullet Punch (60 BP Steel, neutral) and Weavile's super-effective Ice Shard (2x) can KO Dragapult before it fires. Even if Dragapult Protects, we survive to pivot next turn.
Noivern threatens Draco Meteor OHKO on Dragapult per notebook data, removing the immediate Fire-type threat to both our Pokémon. Weavile passes to shake off flinch and reset for next turn's pressure.

Dragapult swaps to Kingambit: Dark/Steel resists Ice Shard (3.9–9.1%) and Draco Meteor (16.4–38.9%), safely tanking both. Incineroar Parting Shots Weavile to −2 Atk/−1 SpA, then pivots to Conkeldurr. This preserves Dragapult's 59%, cripples Weavile's offense, and sets up Kingambit+Conkeldurr with double priority (Sucker Punch, Mach Punch 4× Weavile) next turn. Even if foe predicts and doubles Incineroar, Knock Off (9.8–13.9%) + Draco (34–50%) falls short of KO.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Dragapult+Incineroar lead, Conkeldurr+Kingambit back. Dragapult (213 Spe) outspeeds entire foe team (Weavile 194 max, Noivern 192 max). Weavile/Scizor lack Protect. Opponent's unrevealed fourth is one of {Excadrill, Toxapex, Mamoswine} — Excadrill most likely given their Ice/Steel/Ground core. Kingambit immune to Toxic Spikes, Supreme Overlord gains +10% per fainted ally. Conkeldurr Sheer Force Expert Belt: Mach Punch 4× Weavile, Ice Punch 2× Noivern. Incineroar Sitrus pivot re-applies Intimidate via Parting Shot. Life Orb recoil on Dragapult is manageable; preserve for endgame speed control.

decisions.rationale: Conkeldurr at 100% HP is the safer switch: it resists Weavile's Dark moves and takes manageable damage from -2 foes (Hurricane 31–88% + Ice Shard 6–17% = max 105%, unlikely KO). Mach Punch threatens Weavile (89–248%) with priority; Ice Punch OHKOs Noivern. Kingambit resists all opponent attacks (0.5x from Dark/Ice/Flying) and Iron Head 2HKOs Weavile. Preserves Dragapult for late-game speed control versus the unrevealed Excadrill.

Both target Dragapult to eliminate the fast special attacker at 59%. Weavile's Ice Shard has priority +1 and is super-effective, potentially KOing alone. Noivern's Draco Meteor OHKOs Dragapult per notebook data as insurance. Eliminating Dragapult removes the biggest threat to both Pokémon.

Mach Punch guarantees OHKO on Weavile before it can move; Kowtow Cleave chunks Noivern 47–88%. Weavile Ice Shard (9–14%) + Noivern Hurricane (45–68%) into Conkeldurr falls short of KO. Even if Weavile switches (only 1 bench slot), Mach Punch hits the replacement and Kowtow Cleave still pressures Noivern. Boomburst is negligible (5–9% Kingambit, 14–21% Conk). Supreme Overlord at 1 stack.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Dragapult+Incineroar lead, Conk+Kingambit back. Weavile/Noivern/Scizor all lack Protect. Weavile OHKO'd by Conk Mach Punch (4x, SheerForce+ExpertBelt). Noivern -2 SpA does modest damage. Kingambit Supreme Overlord: +10% per fainted ally (1 now: Scizor). Opponent's 4th unrevealed from {Excadrill,Toxapex,Mamoswine}; Excadrill most likely. Only 1 bench slot remains so at most 1 switch per turn. Dragapult (213 Spe) outspeeds entire foe team; preserve for cleanup. Incineroar Sitrus pivot can reapply Intimidate via Parting Shot.

decisions.rationale: Focus-fire Conkeldurr: Hurricane (2x, 40-80%) + Icicle Crash (neutral, 24-42%) can KO or cripple it before its guaranteed OHKO Close Combat lands on Weavile. Weavile dies next turn regardless, so maximize damage now. If Conkeldurr falls, we get a 2v1 on Kingambit at 62%.

Weavile's Icicle Crash and Noivern's Hurricane are best available damage on Conkeldurr this turn.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Sucker Punch (+1 prio) outspeeds and KOs 14% Noivern before it moves if it attacks (39.1% min). If Noivern Defogs to dodge, Sucker Punch fails but Noivern wastes its turn on a useless Defog. Switch Conkeldurr to Incineroar avoids confusion risk and 37% HP danger; Hurricane into Incineroar does 11.9-39.4% at -2 SpA, easily absorbed with Sitrus. Next turn: Incineroar Fake Out + Kingambit cleans up.

Kingambit Supreme Overlord: +10% per fainted ally (2: Scizor, Weavile). Opponent's 4th revealed as Toxapex (BanefulBunker/Recover/Haze/ToxicSpikes, Bold, Leftovers/Regenerator). Dragapult (213 Spe) outspeeds entire foe team; preserve for cleanup. Incineroar Sitrus pivot can reapply Intimidate via Parting Shot. Toxapex is passive but hard to break without SE damage; Kingambit's Dark STAB is neutral.

decisions.rationale: Hurricane into Conkeldurr is a guaranteed KO (63–88% of max HP at 2× super-effective, vs 36% remaining). Toxic Spikes punishes the opponent's Parting Shot pivot core on every switch, applying passive damage that compounds across the game.

decisions.rationale: Game 1 is unwinnable: Noivern is fainted with no legal switch (Scizor/Weavile also fainted, Excadrill/Mamoswine reserved for games 2-3). Forfeiting preserves series information and lets me debut unrevvealed Pokémon in game 2 where Excadrill and Mamoswine counter the Parting Shot pivot core.

reflections.summary: Opponent brought a fragile hyper-offense team (Scizor, Weavile, Noivern) completely lacking Protect, which our turn-1 Fake Out + Fire Blast eliminated Scizor for free. Parting Shot into Kingambit on turn 2 absorbed the remaining offense while safely pivoting Conkeldurr in. Conkeldurr’s Mach Punch immediately KO’d Weavile, and Kingambit’s Supreme Overlord–boosted Sucker Punch cleaned Noivern before Toxapex could exert any pressure. The opponent’s only durable member, Toxapex, was left alone without offensive support, unable to stop our remaining three Pokémon.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent’s limited Protect and frail compositions, maintain the aggressive lead pairing. If they bring Toxapex again, consider preserving Dragapult’s Life Orb Shadow Ball to break through Toxapex after its partners fall, and use Incineroar’s Parting Shot to pivot safely around Baneful Bunker turns instead of risking contact moves into it.
reflections.notebook: Game 1 opponent brought Scizor/Weavile/Noivern/Toxapex, none of which carried Protect. Scizor and Weavile are very frail: Conkeldurr Mach Punch OHKOs Weavile. Noivern used Draco Meteor turn 2 (-2 SpA), then Hurricane turn 3, lacking Protect; it is vulnerable to Sucker Punch. Opponent’s Noivern outspeeds Conkeldurr but not Dragapult (213). Toxapex set is BanefulBunker/Recover/Haze/Toxic Spikes, Bold, Leftovers, Regenerator; it is passive but we must plan a special attacker or boosting move to break it if it remains as the last Pokémon. Dragapult should be preserved as a win condition against all their fast threats (Noivern, Weavile) and as a breaker for Toxapex. Incineroar can pivot repeatedly with Parting Shot to reapply Intimidate and avoid BanefulBunker traps. Kingambit’s Supreme Overlord bonus increases with each KO; keep it on the back line to receive Parting Shot and clean weakened targets.

reflections.summary: Lost because the team preview plan was poorly matched to the opponent's Parting Shot pivot core. Scizor was OHKO'd by Dragapult's Fire Blast on turn 1, Weavile was worn down by Intimidate/Parting Shot and cleaned up by Conkeldurr's priority, and Noivern was frail and Sucker Punched. The four chosen (Scizor, Weavile, Noivern, Toxapex) lacked a dedicated breaker that could safely handle Incineroar and Kingambit after they set up via pivoting. Toxapex alone could not contest the remaining 100% Incineroar, 62% Kingambit, and 59% Dragapult, leading to a forfeit at turn 5.
reflections.adjustment: Replace Scizor or Toxapex with Excadrill (Mold Breaker Earthquake). Excadrill safely threatens Incineroar, Kingambit, and Conkeldurr — the three physical pillars the opponent relied on — while providing its own pivoting via U-turn and better mid-game offensive pressure against the Parting Shot core.
reflections.notebook: Opponent Parting Shot pivot core confirmed: Incineroar (SitrusBerry, Intimidate, Parting Shot) + Dragapult (LifeOrb, Fire Blast for Scizor/physical lures). Kingambit runs BlackGlasses + SupremeOverlord; Kowtow Cleave and Sucker Punch are key damage moves. Conkeldurr runs ExpertBelt + SheerForce; Mach Punch priority OHKOs Weavile. Talonflame and Serperior remain unused bench threats — Talonflame likely Tailwind/Gale Wings support, Serperior likely Contrary LeafStorm or Taunt. Noivern Draco Meteor is a confirmed Dragapult OHKO. Excadrill and Mamoswine remain series bench options for games 2-3; Excadrill's Mold Breaker Earthquake covers the Incineroar/Kingambit/Conkeldurr triangle safely.
